On a 2560 point wide window a lanes redraw is 8 ms on average (50 ms at p95 with thumbnails coming in), and committing it then waited on the screen to release the last frame: 40% of a paced drag was spent blocked there. The clips the box picks up now get amber outlines on a shape layer, the same as the stroke a selected clip draws, and the lanes don't redraw until the selection lands on mouse up.

title: The editor window opens where it was
paragraphs: Reopening Tandem (as installing a build does) put the editor back at the default size. The window's frame autosave name was set before its window controller took it over, and a window controller clears that name, so no frame was ever saved. AppKit's saving wouldn't have been enough anyway: it puts a window back on whichever screen is active at launch, scaled to fit, not the one it was on.

Tandem now saves the frame itself when the window moves or resizes (not in full screen or minimised) and opens the next window there if it's still on a screen: enough title bar to grab and half the window showing. A second window steps down and right past the first.

title: Smooth selection box, and middle-button drags pan the timeline
paragraphs: Every mouse move of a selection box set the model's selection, even when it hadn't changed. Each set redrew the inspector, laid the window out again and redrew the whole timeline, about 16 ms on the v14 project, so the box lagged. The box now works out its own selection: the lanes redraw only when it takes in or lets go of a clip, the box is a layer that moves without redrawing anything, and the model hears about the selection once, on mouse up. Its start is pinned to a time, so it stays on its clips while the timeline autoscrolls.
A third of the lanes' drawing time went on thumbnail paths, because appendingPathComponent asked the disk whether each one was a folder.
A middle-button drag anywhere on the timeline (clips, empty track, ruler, headers) now pans it like pushing paper: sideways through time, and up and down when the tracks don't all fit.
tandem://simulate drags take button=middle, and interval=<ms> to pace the steps so the app draws between them like it does for a real mouse.

title: Proxies at quality 0.6, so still areas stop crawling
paragraphs: Proxy frames are all keyframes, so their compression noise is new every frame and crawled over still walls and screen text while playing. At 0.45 8x8 blocks of the camera's wall flickered 3.3 times as much as the original (0.69 against 0.21 levels) and still screen text shimmered (0.36 against 0.08). At 0.6: 0.44 and 0.17, for 100 MB a minute of camera (was 34; the original is 104). The proxy version goes to 2 so they rebuild.

title: Paused stills pick up mattes and proxies that finish later
paragraphs: The viewer kept its FrameRenderer until the project changed, and a renderer keeps the composition it first built. A finished matte rebuilt the player but not the stills, so the cutout showed while playing and the full camera frame showed when paused. The still renderer is now replaced on every rebuild.

title: Playback shows the same colours as paused stills and export
paragraphs: The player looked lighter and flatter than paused frames. Its frames were tagged BT.709 with no colour space attached, so AVPlayerLayer used the exact 709 curve and lifted the shadows: black 16 showed as 32 on screen against 14 for stills and 709 files. The compositor now attaches Core Media's 709 colour space, as decoders do; captured on screen, player and still agree within a level (the demo at 35 s: +3.2 levels before, 0.0 now).

The video composition's 709 colour properties also made AVFoundation re-tag every source frame 709 without converting it, so BT.601 footage (Mike's camera) decoded with the wrong matrix: red 180/40/50 came out 192/54/48, skin a few levels green. They're gone, and frames keep their own tags.

PlaybackMatchTests checks player, paused still, tandem frame and export against each other and the source, on colour patches and on a cutout picture in picture with a half-size proxy and matte. RealColourTests, ColourOnScreenTests and ProxyNoiseTests measure the real demo project.

title: RVM makes the cutout by default, without its light rim
paragraphs: Mike picked RVM over the Vision cutout. matteModel now defaults to it, so existing mattes rebuild with RVM (the key changed), and RVM mattes are version 2 because of the edge fix below.

RVM's soft edge applied to the source's own colours left a light rim of the wall around the cap and shoulders, worst over dark UI. The RVM job now chokes the alpha by a pixel at 1080p and clears alpha under 0.3. On the two test ranges the rim's light drops to about a third, 98% of the alpha where hands move stays, fast swipes keep their motion blur, and flicker improves a little (0.066 and 0.062). Two pixels shaved the ear.

If the model can't be downloaded or loaded, the job makes the Vision matte instead and says so in a note that stays on its status. A fallback.json in the entry records the model file's state; once that file changes, the matte is rebuilt once, with no loop if it falls back again. Tests never download the model.

title: Portrait projects, a fill layout and Ken Burns moves for stills
paragraphs: For shorts made from photos: `tandem new --portrait` (or --size WxH) makes a 1080x1920 project, the fill layout covers the whole frame and crops the edges so a landscape photo fills a 9:16 short, and addMotion gives each still an even zoom or pan across the part that overflows the frame (zoomIn, zoomOut, panLeft/Right/Up/Down).

title: Robust Video Matting as an optional matte model
paragraphs: Mike wanted to see RVM next to the version 2 cutout. Its official Core ML export (MobileNetV3, 1280x720) carries a recurrent state from frame to frame, and on the two 20 s test ranges it beats version 2: flicker 0.08 and 0.07 against 0.17 and 0.20, no pop frames against 12 and 14, sharper edge contrast, the mic kept just as well, and none of Vision's one-frame grabs of sofa and desk. Its soft alpha leaves a faint light rim of the wall around the cap. It runs at 40 fps on the GPU, the same as version 2.

AnalysisSettings.matteModel selects it; Vision (version 2) stays the default. RVM mattes have their own cache key and version. The RVM repository is GPL-3.0, so the model is never committed or bundled: RVMModelStore downloads it from the official release on first use into ~/Library/Application Support/Tandem/Models/rvm/ and checks its SHA-256. Tests swap the download for a local copy.

title: The project list resizes and shows a frame from each project
paragraphs: The project list can be resized and opens at the size it was left at. Each project in it and in Open recent has a small icon: a real frame (a tenth of the way in, or the first picture) rendered with FrameRenderer off the main thread, kept at .tandem/<name>.icon.png and refreshed when the project opens without one, when it's saved (at most every two minutes, and only if it changed) and when it's closed. Recent projects without one get it in the background, one at a time; a blank frame or an empty project shows a quiet placeholder. Quitting waits up to 3 s for icons being made, on a run loop timer, and a SIGTERM quit no longer runs inside a main queue block, which could leave quitting stuck.

Test copies set TANDEM_DEFAULTS_SUITE to keep their own recent projects, list size and export speed (and leave AppKit's saved window frames alone), and tandem://window?width=&height= sizes the front window.

title: Tracks are added, named, reordered and deleted from the headers, and the whole top bar drags the window
paragraphs: The corner above the headers has + Track, and a header's menu adds video or audio tracks above or below it, renames in place, moves it up or down and deletes it with its clips (undoable, and links left with one clip are undone). Dragging a name reorders tracks of its kind. New tracks follow ripple edits and open their name for typing; the Timeline menu has Add video track (Cmd-Option-V) and Add audio track (Cmd-Option-A).

Every empty part of the top bar, the title included, now moves the window through performDrag, and a double-click there zooms or minimises as System Settings says. Scripted drags move it by hand, and the input simulator can type into the field with the keys and pick a context menu item by title.

title: A bolder amber icon
paragraphs: The dark icon read as an empty square in the Dock at small sizes. The new one is the Graphite amber with two offset clips and a playhead, legible down to 16 px on light and dark backgrounds.

title: A steadier cutout matte
paragraphs: Mike saw the AI portrait cutout flicker. On two 20 s ranges of his takes the matte changed by 1.5 to 2.2 (of 255) a frame where the picture was still: the person instance blend dropped the mic on up to a sixth of the frames, the accurate mask's outline shimmered and Vision grabbed sofa and desk for a frame at a time.

Matte version 2 blends the person mask with Vision's foreground subject mask, which holds still and keeps the mic, and then smooths over time only where the picture is still (medians of three and seven frames and a gentle average), so moving hands never trail or get cut. Flicker drops to 0.17 and 0.20, frames with pops from 74/130 to 12/14. It runs at 41 fps with four workers against 49 to 52 before.
The old cutout stays selectable (matteProps .personInstances, matteSmoothing .off). Both settings are in the cache key and the matte version is 2, so existing mattes rebuild.

title: Analysis follows the edit, not the whole folder
paragraphs: Opening a project used to queue proxies for every large video in the folder and a matte, transcript and isolated voice for every camera file, which for a folder like decision-models (about 295 files, old renders included) meant hours of work and many GB of cache.

Now everything gets thumbnails, waveforms and loudness, every camera take gets a transcript, and the expensive work only runs for what the edit uses: proxies for large video on the timeline, a matte once a clip's cutout is on (in the clip's cutout mode), isolated voice once a clip uses it, and a transcript for anything on a speech track, so screen-recording audio on the Voice track is searchable too. The app and `tandem serve` re-check after each burst of edits.

title: A save that fails says so, and autosave keeps trying
paragraphs: ProjectSession records why the last save failed (saveProblem), retries a failed autosave every 5 s, and close() returns its final save's error. The app shows the reason in the status bar with a lasting Not saved note and "not saved" in the title, says when saving works again, and asks before closing a window or quitting with edits that won't save.

title: A Finder drop is worked out against the project when it lands
paragraphs: The edit came from the window's copy of the project, which can lag the coordinator: the folder watcher's scan could add a copied file first and the drop would add it again. Now it's built from the coordinator's snapshot with expectedRevision, rebuilt if another commit lands first, and media is matched by where it resolves in the folder (in one Unicode form) as the scan does.

title: Space previews assets, looks and fonts go on clips, Generate makes music
paragraphs: Space over a tile or row in the asset browser opens a big preview over the viewer (stickers and clips loop, sound plays, fonts show their letters); Space again or Escape closes it. Looks (LUTs) and fonts get sub-tabs in the Effects and Text tabs and apply to the clip they're dropped on, or to the selected clips on double-click. Music and SFX have a Generate popover for ElevenLabs with the cost up front and the provider's refusal shown before anyone pays. Import folders are rescanned at launch and watched, and a project's fonts are registered when it opens.

title: Backups that last, and exports that only replace their own
paragraphs: Autosave saves every second or so, so keeping the last 20 backups kept only minutes of history. Backups are now taken at most once a minute and thinned over time: everything from the last hour, one per ten minutes for a day, one per day for 30 days.
An export no longer replaces a file at its path unless it's an earlier Tandem export (one with a .tandem snapshot beside it), so an old Filmora render or a download can't be overwritten by accident.

title: Word the interrupted error for event streams too
An unreadable project says where its backups are
paragraphs: A .tandem cut short by a crash or broken by a hand edit failed to open with only the decoder's complaint. The error now names the newest backup in .tandem/backups/ and how to go back to it.

title: Idempotency keys hold between the app and the CLI
paragraphs: The docs promise that a batch retried with the same idempotencyKey returns the first result instead of applying twice. The app kept its keys in memory only and the CLI only checked the ones it had written, so a retry that crossed over (the app quit before the agent heard back and the retry reached the CLI, or the other way round) applied the edit again. Every mode now checks and records keys in the history on disk.

title: Two media scans at once add a new file once
paragraphs: Opening a project in the app starts two scans together (the window's and the folder watcher's first look). Each gave a new file its own random media ID and both added it, so every take recorded while Tandem was closed showed up twice. A refresh now works out its edit against the project as it is when it applies it, skipping files already there and media removed meanwhile, and works it out again if the project changed in between.

title: An edit cut off when the app quits isn't sent twice
paragraphs: When the app (or `tandem serve`) quit or crashed after taking an edit but before answering, the dropped connection came back as "unavailable" and ProjectClient sent the call again, now headless, on top of the saved (or journal-recovered) project that already had it: `tandem apply` applied twice, `tandem undo` undid two steps. A connection that drops mid-call is now "interrupted": reads are still retried, edits are not and say to check `tandem history`. Only a connection that never got through counts as unavailable.

title: Drop files and folders from Finder onto the timeline or the media
paragraphs: Dropped files already in the project folder are used where they are; others are copied in by kind (broll/, graphics/, audio/), an APFS clone on the same disk, or linked from linked-media/ when they're on another disk. They're probed and join the project in one edit that reuses any media the folder watcher added first; on the timeline they're placed one after another from the drop point (a single file on a track goes on that track). The media browser takes drops through an AppKit drop zone, and tandem://simulate can drop files for checks.

title: Saves follow a video folder renamed while it's open
paragraphs: Renaming or moving the video folder in Finder with the project open left the session saving to the old path. Usually that failed quietly (autosave and close swallow the error, the journal couldn't be written either), so every edit after the rename was gone on quit; and if the analysis cache had recreated the old path, the project was saved into that stray folder instead of the renamed one. The session and the journal now hold a descriptor on their folder and ask the system where it is (F_GETPATH) when they write, and the lock is removed from where it ended up. Media paths still resolve against the old folder until the project is opened again.

title: An import that won't replace a project says why plainly
paragraphs: Opening an import in the app can move it to revision 1 without an edit (the media scan fills in fingerprints), so say it has changed and may hold edits rather than that it has been edited.

title: A media refresh patches only what the scan changed
paragraphs: refreshMedia sent each changed item whole as its updateMedia patch, and updateMedia refuses a patch with an "id" in it, so any refresh that had to update a known file failed as a whole and added nothing. Imported projects always hit this (their media has no fingerprint yet), as does any project once a file it knows changes on disk: new takes and sounds then never joined the project, and the app's rescans failed silently. The patch is now the difference between the item before and after the scan, which also keeps an edit made to the same media while the scan ran (a look, a role) instead of reverting it.

title: A damaged journal line costs only itself
paragraphs:
Three ways the crash-recovery journal lost edits:
- Reading it as one UTF-8 string meant a last line cut short in the middle of a character (a crash, a full disk) made every entry unreadable, so nothing was recovered. Lines are now read one by one.
- An append after a cut-short line joined it, and both were lost. An append now starts a new line after one without an ending.
- When the journal couldn't be opened for appending, the fallback wrote the new entry atomically over the whole journal. Appends now go through open(O_APPEND | O_CREAT) and never replace it; a failed write also returns an error instead of FileHandle's exception on a full disk, which crashed the app mid-edit.

title: Frames and screenshots never overwrite media or a project
paragraphs: Exports refused to replace the project's media, but `frame -o` and `screenshot -o` (CLI, HTTP and MCP) wrote their PNG over any path: `tandem frame 12 -o source/take-camera.mov` replaced the camera take, and `-o Video.tandem` replaced the project. The export check is now shared as RenderOutputs and also refuses .tandem files; frames, screenshots, exports and review clips all go through it, the renders before they start.

title: Keyframe editing, and background commands leave focus alone
paragraphs: Keyframes show as diamonds on clips (gain ones on the volume line, which now follows the animated level). Click one to choose it and move the playhead there, drag it to move it (gain diamonds also set the level, Shift keeps the time), right-click for easing, Delete removes it. Option-K adds or removes keyframes at the playhead, Shift-J and Shift-K step between them. The inspector shows animated values at the playhead, a diamond beside every animatable control, and an Animation section with the easing of the keyframe under the playhead. Changing an animated value, in the inspector or by dragging in the viewer, keys it at the playhead. Every change is a setKeyframes batch.
The app no longer activates itself at launch, so open -g launches and tandem:// commands leave Mike's front app in front.

title: Using an asset again never replaces a different file
paragraphs: Using an asset copies it to assets/<kind>/<name>-<code>.<ext>. When a file of that name was already there with a different size, it was deleted and replaced with the library's file: a copy Mike had reworked, or the one the timeline was playing before the library's file changed. The new copy now goes beside it under the next free name, and a copy that matches is reused as before.

title: Importing again never replaces an edited project
paragraphs: `tandem import` wrote <out>/<name>/<name>.tandem whether or not it was there, so re-running an import after editing the result replaced the edited project with a fresh import (only a backup kept, and that is pruned after 20 saves). An import now replaces an earlier one only while it is untouched: revision 0 and nothing unsaved in its journal. Otherwise it stops and says to use --name or move the file.

title: A new project file doesn't inherit an old one's journal
paragraphs: A deleted project leaves .tandem/<name>.journal.jsonl and .undo.json behind. `tandem new` and New Project in the app create the same name again (it comes from the folder), and opening the new file replayed the old journal over it: with an undo snapshot in there, the new project came up as the old one. The undo history could likewise restore an old timeline once the revisions lined up. Creating a project and Save As now clear both.

title: A save clears only the journal entries it wrote
paragraphs: save() took its snapshot, wrote the file, then emptied the journal. An edit that committed while the file was being written (an agent's call, a drag in the app) wasn't in the file, and emptying the journal threw its entry away too, so a crash before the next autosave lost it. The journal now keeps entries newer than the revision that was saved.

title: Journal the project a reload puts in place
paragraphs: An agent's `tandem undo` through the app falls back to the undo history kept on disk for CLI edits, which restores the project with coordinator.reload. Reload didn't write to the journal, so if the app then died before autosaving, recovery replayed the edits made after the undo on top of the file's old state: the undone edit came back and the later batches landed on the wrong timeline. Reload now appends a snapshot, like undo and redo do.

title: Pruning backups leaves other versions' backups alone
paragraphs: Saving Video.tandem pruned every backup whose name started with "Video ", which includes a Save As version's ("Video v2 <stamp>"). Those sort after Video's own, so with a busy v2 in the folder, saving Video deleted all of Video's backups, including the one just made. Backups now count only when the rest of the name is a backup stamp.

title: Paused frames come from the originals again
paragraphs: The render module now decodes the frames remuxed open-GOP files can't seek to, so the viewer lays full-resolution stills over the proxy player when paused.

title: Say what PitchShift.effect returns
PitchShift audio effect
paragraphs: A clip's sound is rendered once through Apple's time-pitch unit (offline, with keyframed semitones applied per slice) into a cached copy, and the composition plays the copy. Offline the unit adds no delay, so sync is untouched, and speed changes still keep the shifted pitch. Tests check an octave up (880 Hz, same length, a silent gap still in place to 12 ms) and a keyframed ramp.

title: Exact frames from remuxed open-GOP HEVC, never black or stalled
paragraphs: Frame grabs and a paused player on originals came back black at some times, for example 404 s of the v14 edit. The cause isn't variable frame rate gaps (AVFoundation holds the last frame through those): it's open-GOP HEVC whose keyframes lost their sync sample group when remuxed by ffmpeg, as with decision-models' edit/main-screen.mov. AVFoundation then starts decoding at a CRA keyframe when it seeks into the frames that lead up to it, and they fail: grabs get nothing, a cut into them repeats the previous clip's frame, and a reader starting on them stalls forever.

LeadingFrameMap reads the sample tables to find those windows. Segments that start inside one go into the composition from its keyframe, FrameRecovery decodes the frames left out (and any AVFoundation couldn't supply) from a little earlier, range exports starting inside one read from just before it, and a stalled export fails after two minutes instead of hanging. Tests use a synthetic open-GOP file with its sync group stripped and a 10 s gap; on the real footage every hard frame of v14 now matches Filmora's export.

title: Tandem://assets can pick the scope
Logos that size in em and short hex colours draw, and library copies show their asset's name
Asset browser, titles, transitions and effects libraries
paragraphs: Audio and Graphics browse the asset library (music, SFX, stickers, icons and logos, B-roll): catalogue search as you type, Return asks the online sources, favourites, recent, downloaded and in-project scopes, source chips, licence and length filters, licence on every tile, hover previews (stickers and video scrub, audio plays from the hovered point of its waveform), a Credits popover to copy, and import folders. The starter set goes in on first launch. Double-click places at the playhead and dragging places at the drop point, as one edit through AssetLibrary.use and the placement's commands.

Text has the render module's title styles and three templates; Effects and Transitions share a panel with tiles previewed on the current frame and transitions you use most. All of them drag onto the timeline: a transition onto a cut, an effect onto a clip.

title: WIP: frame recovery for undecodable leading frames
9:16 shorts from the same edit
paragraphs: setFormatLayout places video clips in an alternate output format (top half, bottom half or full frame, filled edge to edge) and can turn the cutout off there. `tandem short` (and the short MCP tool) adds the portrait format and lays out every clip the way Mike's shorts look: screen on top, camera below with its background. The landscape edit is untouched and `tandem export --preset short` renders the short.

title: Word-by-word captions from the transcripts
paragraphs: `tandem captions` (and the captions MCP tool and HTTP operation) plans caption clips a few words at a time, breaking at sentence ends and pauses, frame aligned and never overlapping, with word timings so the caption preset highlights the word being spoken. They go on a Captions track that follows ripple edits. A dry run unless --apply.

title: The agent chip knows exactly who's connected
paragraphs: TandemService.onCall reports every call (reads included) with its author, EventHub.subscriberCount counts open watch streams, and the client sends its author on watch. The app marks an agent connected on any call in the last five minutes or while it watches.

title: Launcher, setup script, icon and README entries
paragraphs: `tandem app` opens the editor and every other `tandem` command goes to the agent CLI in the app bundle. setup_mac.sh builds the release app, install_mac.sh links the launcher, and the repo README lists the tool.

title: Tandem screenshot saves the app window
paragraphs: The service and MCP could already capture the app window; the CLI now can too, and explains when no app has the project open.

title: Release builds find the keymap; test bundles stay out of the app
paragraphs: Release builds lay the resource bundle out with Contents/Resources, so the flat path lookup missed the keymap. build-app.sh also copied test fixture bundles into the app.

title: Captures include popovers, and debug shows how long a new cut takes to appear
Kill quits cleanly, and captures never show a frame from another time
Paused frames stay on the player until grabs fill VFR gaps
paragraphs: Exact grabs from the originals come back black in a screen recording's variable frame rate gaps (v14 at 6:44), while proxies and exports are right, so the still over a paused player is off behind a flag.

title: A simulated menu dump only writes text files
The viewer's frame reader takes the compositor's format
Real thumbnails, waveforms, transcripts and job progress
paragraphs: Thumbnails decode off the main thread at draw size (lanes back to 2.5 ms a draw on the 494 clip v14 import), the transcript lane shows every few phrases when zoomed out and refreshes when a transcript lands, finished proxies and mattes rebuild the preview, proxy playback composites at 1080p, and the status bar names jobs by take time and quietly lists what the preview can't show yet.

title: Asset library for agents, and render warnings in results
paragraphs: tandem assets providers, search, fetch, use, credits, generate and install-starter, with matching MCP tools (assets_search, assets_use, assets_credits, assets_generate, assets_providers). use copies the asset into the project through AssetLibrary.use and applies the placement's edit through ProjectClient, so it lands in the app when the app has the project open, and reuses a media item the app's folder watcher already made for the copied file. The library is per user; TANDEM_ASSETS_ROOT moves it and TANDEM_ASSETS_OFFLINE=1 keeps it off the network and out of the Keychain.
Frame, clip and export results now carry the renderer's warnings (a camera shown without its cutout because the matte isn't made yet), kept to the media and clips that play in what was rendered.

title: CLI tests wait for processes without waitUntilExit
paragraphs: waitUntilExit spins the run loop of the thread that launched the process, so an async test that resumed on another thread could wait forever for tandem serve or tandem mcp to exit. A termination handler signals instead.

title: Host the API while a project is open
paragraphs: Each window serves the local API through TandemAPIHost, opens with the waiting ProjectSession.open when a CLI command or tandem serve has the file, captures itself for the API's screenshot, and stops the host before the session closes. The agent chip follows agents: connected, is editing §2, edited 11:42. The library tabs stay centred, and the copied MCP config passes --project.

title: Crash-free export cancel and mode-aware cutout mattes
paragraphs: Cancelling an AVAssetReader while another thread is inside copyNextSampleBuffer crashes AVFoundation, and an output read after its reader is released does too. Cancel is now a flag: the encoder feed and the muxers stop at the next sample, the feed thread (which keeps the reader alive) is joined on every exit path, and only then is the reader cancelled. The test cancels during the loudness pass, just after encoding starts, midway and near the end.
Cutouts use the matte made in their own mode (matteURL(for:mode:)) and fall back to the default matte. The internal export job is renamed ExportPipeline, since the API has a public ExportJob.

title: Long-lived sessions watch the folder and start analysis
paragraphs: The app and `tandem serve` now start background analysis for the project's media (timeline media first) and add files that land in the folder. One-shot CLI commands don't. The API reads readiness from the analysis cache instead of loading each result.

title: Removing a folder mid-scan leaves nothing, fetches follow a changed note, watcher reports once
Test that the viewer's player item plays through the compositor
Iconify pages cover every result; word forms match whole words only
Refuse export outputs that could destroy work
paragraphs: An export to one of the project's own media files would delete it before reading, and an output without a movie extension would put its snapshot at the project's own file name. Both are refused with a clear message. The shared black base movie is recreated if the temporary folder is cleaned and tolerates two processes making it at once.

title: Note the staging folder in the layout docs
Versions saved elsewhere keep their media; tandem:// links write only their own file types
paragraphs: New project and Save As are split from their panels, so tandem://new and tandem://version can drive them. A version opens before the old window closes, and a replaced file's stale journal is cleared.

title: Export tests for pitch-kept speed changes and voice isolation
Test that a failed scan doesn't jam the scan queue
Tandem import filmora, edl and compare
paragraphs: Wires the importer into the CLI: Filmora projects and agent EDLs become .tandem projects with a report beside them, and compare shows how two cuts of the same take differ. Options can now repeat (--search, --rewrite).

title: Check whether matte workers upset Vision's temporal state
paragraphs: VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest is a stateful request, and the three matte workers each see a timing-dependent share of the frames, so the review asked whether mattes vary run to run. An opt-in experiment (TANDEM_MATTE_EXPERIMENT=1) builds 20 s of the camera five ways: shared workers twice, a fresh request per frame twice, and one worker in order. All five mattes are identical to the byte, so the pipeline stays as it is; the stateless option is kept for the experiment.

title: Loudness in the export snapshot, muted clips never join seamlessly
Give up on a busy video encoder after two minutes instead of hanging
One-pass loudness correction, render notes, alpha test
paragraphs: The limited loudness pass runs four candidate gains side by side on one decode and interpolates the target, instead of up to three sequential passes. The exporter cancels its reader on any failure after encoding starts and records phase timings for benchmarks. docs/RENDER.md explains the render module's rules, conventions and measured speeds, and a test covers HEVC-with-alpha overlays.

title: Repeated frame times and planar speech formats
paragraphs:
- A frame whose time isn't after the previous one (a duplicate in a damaged file) is dropped rather than failing the whole proxy or matte; VideoToolbox refuses time going backwards.
- Speech audio is written channel by channel when the analyzer's format is planar with more than one channel, instead of overrunning channel 0. Today's format is mono, so this was latent.

title: Loudness sums clip levels up per track
paragraphs: On the imported v14 edit every voice clip has its own gain, so the text form now gives each track's clip count, gain spread and most common gain instead of 160 lines. The JSON still lists every clip.

title: No duplicate licence snapshots when the terms haven't changed
Evicted cache entries are renamed away before deletion
paragraphs: Deleting an entry in place let a lookup see its manifest after the proxy inside was gone. Entries are now renamed to a temporary name first (which lookups ignore and cleanup removes) and then deleted.

title: Watcher settles files by the Mac's clock
paragraphs: A file had to be older than the settle time by its own date, so one dated in the future (a camera clock ahead) was never reported, and a copy keeping an old date could be reported while still growing. Files now settle once their size and date stop changing for the settle time. The snapshot is taken after the stream starts, so a file created during start is either in it or in an event.

title: No orphaned asset folders, keep downloads when normalising fails, safe watcher callbacks
Known media in skipped folders stays in the project
paragraphs: A known item inside the project but in a folder the walk skips (an imported render in exports/, a hidden folder) was marked missing on every scan, and a copy of the file could take its ID. Every known item the walk didn't reach is now checked at its own path.

title: Waveform buckets exact at 22.05 and 11.025 kHz
paragraphs: The bucket size was rounded to whole samples (221 for 220.5), so peaks drifted 0.2% early: a click at 500 s landed at 498.86 s. Bucket edges are now worked out in floating point. Progress reports how far the peaks have got rather than the pre-sized array, and samples stamped before zero are skipped.

title: Short badges like Full always draw
Iconify pages never overlap
Isolated voice is never longer than its source
paragraphs: The render in which the input ran out could reach past its end, and that tail was written, so voice.caf came out up to a render's worth too long (69,732 frames became 70,063 in review). Writes now stop at the source's length. Mono sources report 2,705 samples of latency against 3,665 in stereo; the real-footage test now checks a mono minute lines up too (within a sample, like stereo).

title: Fonts and LUTs count towards a project's credits
Timeline view tuned on a real imported edit
paragraphs: Settings most of a track's clips share are said once in the track line and each clip lists only its differences, so a PiP camera track no longer repeats its layout on every line. --summary gives one line per track for finding your way round a long edit. Checked on the imported decision-models v14 (494 clips): the full view drops from 67 KB of repetition to 61 KB, and the summary is 20 lines.

title: Calmer and faster timeline on real projects
paragraphs: Checked against the imported decision-models v14 (494 clips, 12 tracks): transition chips shrink with the clips beside them and fades draw as ramps, labels that would truncate to a letter are left out, names sit in badges instead of shadowed text, slivers draw as plain bars, and text widths and names are cached. A full redraw of the lanes takes about 2 ms on average (3.5 ms p95) in a release build. tandem://debug now reports draw timings. Unpaired record-it files read as "Camera · 10:54" in the browser, and track names use the header's full width until the toggles show.

title: Keep every paid ElevenLabs take when a later one fails
paragraphs: A bad key is no longer remembered as a missing permission, and the PCM channel guess only says stereo for a body close to twice the mono size.

title: Scheduler fixes from review
paragraphs:
- A job's context now holds the encoder lock itself, and the scheduler cancels what's left when it goes away. Before, closing a project while a proxy or matte was building left EncoderLock.shared busy for good, so every later export waited forever.
- Cancelling a queued job removes it in the same critical section that finds it, so it can't be started meanwhile, and a finishing job only removes its own entry, never a resubmitted job with the same ID.
- A job only steps aside when that lets the waiting job start. With two encoder slots a matte paused and resumed at every checkpoint (47 times in the new test) for a proxy blocked by the proxy limit.

title: Import folders follow note changes, survive unreadable folders and never scan twice at once
Warning-free render tests
Gentler cut slide, cross zoom and more render coverage
paragraphs: Cut slide keeps a hint of motion blur instead of a smear, and zoom is a cross zoom that always fills the frame. New tests cover every push and slide direction, text alignment and line spacing, keyframed position, scaled frame grabs, AVFoundation's validation of the video composition and preset size overrides.

title: Test that analysis job updates reach watchers
Previews, eviction and missing files never overwrite a newer row
Pruning and provider searches keep the starter set
Real-footage render checks and Filmora-matched grade
paragraphs: Opt-in tests (TANDEM_REAL_MEDIA=1) export a 4K minute of the decision models screen with the cutout PiP camera, grade, shadow, voice and music (3.7x real time), time a 60 s range of the imported v14 edit (4.2x), and compare frames with Filmora's v14 export side by side. The vignette fall-off and black level strength are calibrated to that export.

title: Search as you type, with word forms instead of a stemmer
Transcripts drop audio stamped before the start
paragraphs: Priming samples a decoder stamps before zero (or before a range's start) are dropped before they reach SpeechAnalyzer and the loudness envelope, so word times stay in media time.

title: Voice isolation can't spin forever on a stalled render
Isolated voice drops audio stamped before zero
paragraphs: If a decoder hands out priming samples with negative time stamps, they are now dropped (across as many chunks as they span) instead of shifting the whole result later, so sample n still matches the original's.

title: Keep sticker timing when a frame won't decode, refresh cached keys
Drag a track's bottom edge to resize it
paragraphs: Double-click the edge to go back to the standard height. The split handle sets its cursor instead of pushing onto the cursor stack.

title: Cache and export churn no longer makes the watcher rescan
paragraphs: Every committed analysis renames a folder inside .tandem/cache, and each folder event under the project made the watcher walk the whole folder. Folder events inside skipped folders (and for the skipped folders themselves) are now ignored, and unrelated events no longer push back reports that are due.

title: Test that CLI-facing results encode as JSON
Transitions into stills don't need handles
paragraphs: The importer found two-sided transitions into images being rejected: a still can show any amount of itself, so only moving media needs frames before the cut.

title: Window ownership, held keys in input replay
paragraphs: Project and welcome windows aren't released by AppKit behind their controllers' backs, an unused change hook is gone, and tandem://simulate can hold Z so the viewer's zoom rectangle can be exercised.

title: Test the API under parallel requests
Exporter with VideoToolbox encode and mastered loudness
paragraphs: Composed frames go to a hardware VTCompressionSession (HEVC or H.264, speed priority, preset bitrate, BT.709 video range) and AVAssetWriter. The mix is measured in audio-only passes, gained to the loudness target and run through the true-peak limiter with its delay compensated, then encoded as AAC 48 kHz stereo. Range export, progress, cancel, silent audio for picture-only timelines and a project snapshot beside the file. Tests cover sync of a flash and a beep, loudness within 0.5 LU, colour tags, formats and cancellation.

title: Key the search index on a declared rowid so VACUUM can't break it
An open for the app that waits for the CLI
paragraphs: ProjectSession.open(_:owner:waitingUpTo:) waits out a CLI command that has the project for a moment and asks tandem serve to let go, so the app can open a project an agent is working on.

title: Edit text clips in the inspector, clip tooltips
paragraphs: Text clips get their words, size, weight, colour, background and shadow in the Video tab (colour pickers commit once they settle); the cutout section only shows for media. Hovering a clip shows its track, name, times, layout and speed.

title: Refresh day-old Pixabay links by ID before downloading
Tests for import edge cases
paragraphs: Covers the builder retrying a rejected batch command by command, track families growing lanes, Filmora clips that meet (either end convention) still meeting and real overlaps moving to an extra track, EDL overlays on the EDL's own timeline, screen offsets, segments cut at the end of their recording session and cut adjustments that match nothing.

title: Theme holds every colour; takes named when unbadged
Keep API helpers off other modules' types
paragraphs: MediaAnalysis is wrapped by MediaAnalysisSource instead of extended, command summaries live in CommandText and preset lookup in PresetNames, so nothing clashes when the media, render or core branches add methods of the same name.

title: Resume font registration exactly once
Time the watcher settle test from the last write
paragraphs: The test measured the settle delay from after its final sleep, 0.2 s after the last write, so it could fail by a couple of milliseconds. It now measures from the write itself.

title: Flag titles still holding Filmora's placeholder text
paragraphs: Decision Models v14 has two "Text Here" titles from a Basic 1 template, one of them visible in the exported video at 10:34. The report now calls out any title that still says Filmora's default text.

title: Rescan the folder on focus, capture the player's frame
paragraphs: New files in the project folder show up when the project opens and when its window comes back to the front. Window captures draw the player's current frame (read back through AVPlayerItemVideoOutput) where the video layer is, so screenshots show real pictures once the render module builds compositions. Checked against a real asset in a player.

title: A matte job fails cleanly when it can't get a frame buffer
paragraphs: A frame Vision failed on before any succeeded needs a blank matte from the pool; if the pool and a one-off allocation both fail, the job now stops with an error instead of crashing on a force unwrap.

title: Note missing transcripts once in the timeline view
paragraphs: timeline --words says which files have no transcript yet under the header instead of under every clip, and headless calls key projects by their resolved path so /tmp and /private/tmp share one open project.

title: Singular wording in credit warnings
Layout names match TandemCore's presets
paragraphs: The EDL rebuild marks its PiP clips pipRight (the name the tandem branch's LayoutPreset uses) instead of corner, and imported Filmora camera clips get full, pipRight or pipLeft when their transform says so, so the inspector shows which layout a clip is in.

title: Tandem serve lets go when the app asks
paragraphs: POST /v1/release makes tandem serve save and quit, so the app can open a project an agent session was serving. TandemAPIHost.askOwnerToRelease does the asking and waits for the lock to clear. The app itself refuses release requests.

title: Test similar sounds and font registration through the library
Composition builder, AVFoundation compositor and frame grabs
paragraphs: CompositionBuilder turns the render plan into an AVMutableComposition with a pooled A/B video track layout, matte tracks, speed and freeze mapping, a black base track, TandemInstruction stacks and an audio mix with the planned volume envelopes. FrameRenderer grabs exact frames through the same compositor with RGBA output. End-to-end tests use synthetic movies with frame-number stripes.

title: An emoji in a search finds its sticker
Share model schemas through $defs
paragraphs: The apply tool's input schema drops from 58 KB to 31 KB by writing each model (Clip, Effect, MediaItem...) once under $defs and referring to it with $ref. The validator follows the references.

title: Test that requestDefaults queues timeline media first
Test that generated assets survive eviction
Inspector follows the playhead in a multi-selection
ImportRequest for the CLI, report title and clip animations
paragraphs: ImportRequest runs one import end to end (Filmora or EDL), searching the project's own folder, linking library files next to the output, and writing the project with its report, so `tandem import` only has to parse arguments. Title effects (Text Dropout and friends) and clip in and out animations are now listed in the report instead of vanishing.

title: List an SVGL file once when both themes share it
Request an analysis with other settings
paragraphs: submit, waitFor and state take optional settings, so the render module can ask for a person-only matte for a clip whose cutout mode wants one and read it back with matteURL(for:mode:), without changing the project-wide defaults.

title: Input replay for smoke tests, Cmd-drag insert, focus fixes
paragraphs: tandem://simulate replays clicks, drags, scrolls and context menus into the window through AppKit's own mouse methods, so the timeline and viewer can be exercised without screen control; it found that Cmd at mouse down was treated as a selection toggle, so Cmd-click now toggles on mouse up and Cmd-drag inserts. The inspector follows the clip you clicked in a linked group, clicking editing views takes the keys back from text fields, and small layout fixes from the screenshots.

title: Readable output that scales to a real edit
paragraphs: Big batches list the first dozen created IDs, loudness groups clip levels by setting instead of one line per clip, and media lists only the analyses that have started. Checked on a 420-clip rough cut of decision-models built through the CLI.

title: Tidy the EDL importer, note the recipe's choices
paragraphs: Drops a wrapper struct and a redundant fade line, and adds two notes to the decision-models recipe: the rebuild runs at the footage's 30 fps where v14 was 25 fps, and it keeps voice cuts clean where v14's audio fades at layout switches let cut-out words through.

title: Give large downloads an hour
Map the browser's left rail to asset kinds
Split Filmora assembly out, fix clipped template edges
paragraphs: Moves laying clips on tracks and building the project into FilmoraAssembly.swift. A clip cut short by its template's window no longer inherits a transition from the edge that was cut off, keyframes inside templates are keyed to where the clip starts in its media, and lane trims keep fades within the clip.

title: Looping ElevenLabs effects come as MP3
API review fixes
paragraphs: Change events get their own buffer so job progress can't crowd edits out of history and watch; status reports the on-disk undo history the same way undo uses it; HTTP connections that never finish a request are dropped after 30 s; MCP answers JSON-RPC batches with one array.

title: Probe tests on generated media, frame rate from the peak rate
paragraphs: Tests the AVFoundation probe on a WAV, a WAV named .cof, a PNG with alpha and two small H.264 movies written on the spot (one steady, one sparse like a screen recording), so no media is committed. The frame rate now comes from the shortest frame duration, which is the rate a file records at: the average undercounted a camera file with dropped frames as 29.97.

title: JSON round-trip and accent tests, quicker audio fixtures
Nest the analysis state enum and stop stray thumbnail decodes
paragraphs: The API module declares its own public AnalysisState for JSON, so a second top-level one in TandemMedia would make the name ambiguous in the app and CLI, which import both. It's now MediaAnalysis.ResultState. Thumbnail jobs cancel outstanding image generation when they end early.

title: Agent guide with every edit command and recipes
paragraphs: docs/AGENTS.md covers CLI, MCP and HTTP setup, how batches, revisions and undo work, ripple modes in plain words, an example of every edit command and recipes for the common jobs. A test decodes every JSON example in it.

title: Compare two cuts of the same footage
paragraphs: CutComparison matches voice clips by camera file and source range and reports durations, clip and transition counts, how far matched clips have drifted and where named anchors (section starts) land in each cut. The real decision-models test now writes the EDL rebuild's comparison with the imported v14 beside the project: 122 of v14's 129 voice clips match, the rest are Mike's hand trims in Filmora.

title: Check LUTs on import and preview them before and after
Media notes, and stale temporaries judged by their newest file
paragraphs: docs/MEDIA.md describes scanning, take pairing and the take.json sidecar, the watcher, the cache layout, the scheduler rules, every result format (including the matte and isolated voice contracts the render module reads) and the speeds measured on the decision-models footage.
A temporary folder is only removed as stale when nothing inside it has changed for an hour, so another process's long matte build isn't deleted because its folder date is old.

title: Exact Filmora speeds and mapping tests
paragraphs: Takes a clip's speed from Filmora's own speed curve when it's one speed throughout, since dividing the source range (which carries Filmora's inclusive-end rounding) gave 0.99999999 and would have made every clip a speed change. Adds unit tests for speed, transition names, the colour grade, title colours and weights, keyframe units and file paths.

title: Fit the timeline's tracks, tidy labels, test key routing
paragraphs: The workspace starts short enough for every track to show on a laptop screen, marker labels stop before the next marker, numbers in the UI skip locale grouping, and the look counts only picture clips. Key routing is split from NSEvent so K-hold stepping, Z-hold zoom and repeat filtering are tested.

title: Centre and fit the font sample thumbnail
Local HTTP API, tandem CLI and MCP server
paragraphs: The API serves each operation at POST /v1/<name> on 127.0.0.1 with a bearer token and streams changes as server-sent events at /v1/watch. The CLI and MCP server go through ProjectClient, which talks to the app when it has the project open and otherwise opens the file for just that call. The MCP server speaks both the initialize handshake and the stateless 2026-07-28 revision. The project lock is now held with flock, so a crash can't leave a project locked and parallel commands can't both win it.

title: A matte steps aside for cheaper work in its slot
paragraphs: A new take's proxy used to wait behind the previous take's 15 minute matte because they share the encoder slot and had the same priority. Long jobs now also yield at a checkpoint to waiting jobs of the same priority whose kind goes first (proxy before matte), never to the same kind. Scanning also matches known items by folder-relative path, so an absolute path to a file inside the project (from an import) keeps its ID and becomes relative.
A real-footage test runs every default analysis for a 43 s record-it take through the scheduler at background priority: 33 s in all, the matte being the long pole.

title: Filmora import holds up across the audit corpus
paragraphs: Imports all 119 projects in the Filmora audit corpus with no failed steps. Media Filmora kept no record of stays offline with what the clips say about it instead of being dropped; templates hand their transitions to the layers at their edges; clips too short for the sample grid are skipped; audio lanes without a clear role are named after their video track. Adds opt-in tests to import a whole corpus or print one report.

title: Keep asset folders straight when the library sits under /private
Never let a Keychain prompt hang a headless run
Tests for the activity log, catalog, URL commands and more
paragraphs: Covers the activity feed's mirror of the undo stack, recent projects and version names, media grouping and search (phrases before words), the tandem:// command parser, pause tightening from a transcript, the canvas transform maths shared with the viewer, and the inspector's patches.

title: Tidy import scanning and document the public API
Real footage checks for the media jobs
paragraphs: Opt-in tests on the decision-models footage (TANDEM_REAL_MEDIA=1, run in release with -enable-testing), writing timings to /private/tmp/claude-501/tandem-media/real/report.txt:

- scan: 295 files in 0.43 s, rescan 0.01 s; camera 30 fps CFR, screen VFR, takes paired
- loudness of the 24 min camera: -32.11 LUFS, LRA 11.75, TP -5.30 against ffmpeg's -32.1 / 11.8 / -5.3, in about a second (the meter is now fed 32k-frame blocks rather than decoder-sized ones)
- proxy: 489 fps for 4K camera and VFR screen alike, every frame at its source time; background QoS runs at the same speed
- matte: 49 fps with the instance-mask blend (about 15 min for a 24 min take), cutout stills written for review
- transcript: 65x realtime for a minute, the whole take in 11 s at 53 MB peak; word starts within 80 ms (median) of Whisper medium.en, and snapping word edges finds 5.4 of Whisper's 6.9 s of pauses (1 pause without it)
- isolated voice: 38x realtime, within 1 sample of the original

title: Filmora .wfp importer
paragraphs: Reads zipped or unzipped .wfp projects and rebuilds them through the coordinator. Tracks keep Filmora's layering and get names from what they hold; clips keep times, source ranges and speed (from speed.offset, since Filmora divides in and out points by the speed). Transform and its keyframes, cutout, opacity, crop, drop shadow, border, sharpen, volume, loudness gain and fades map across; a grade every clip of a file shares moves onto the media look. Transitions map onto Tandem's types with their durations, shortened when the media has no handles. Titles become text clips, templates are flattened into their layers and sounds, markers come across, and pictures stay linked with their sound and their take.

Missing files are relinked from rewrites, search folders and Filmora's library on this Mac, or kept offline with the length Filmora recorded. Library MP3s saved as .cof get a linked .mp3 name. WebM stickers become to-do markers. Everything else goes in the report.

title: Remove unkept generated takes from the library
Graphite window, AppKit timeline, viewer, inspector and export
paragraphs: The app shell: AppKit lifecycle with SwiftUI panels, projects opened from the command line, Finder, open -a, File > Open and the recent list, New Project in a folder, Save As for versions, and a welcome window.

The window follows the Graphite design: top bar with library tabs, media browser grouped into takes, graphics, B-roll, music and SFX, the viewer (a layout schematic until the render module lands, then AVPlayer), the inspector (layout, transform, cutout, crop, effects from the registry, the file's look, audio, info, transitions) and the activity feed.

The timeline is layer-backed AppKit: ruler with markers and in/out, track headers with lock, hide and mute, clips drawn per lane style with layout badges, zoom bands, transitions, a transcript lane, snapping, every tool's drag previewed on a copy of the project and committed as one batch, drops from the media browser, and context menus.

Keys go through the JSON keymap from a window-level monitor, so the Premiere single-key shortcuts work wherever the pointer is. tandem:// URLs take screenshots and drive commands for smoke tests and agents. Also fixes build-app.sh when a signing identity exists (empty array expansion under set -u).

title: Evict unpinned files, rebuild the catalogue from meta.json, edit commands for placements
Keep 48 kHz PCM and long beds as they are, measuring only
Opt-in live tests against the real providers
Library facade, import folders, project use, credits and starter set
Pull transcript word edges in to the voice
paragraphs: SpeechAnalyzer's word ranges swallow the silence around them (the spike measured 8.7 of 11.7 s of pauses covered, against 5.1 for Whisper), so the pauses Tandem is meant to tighten would be hidden. While feeding the analyzer, keep a 100 Hz loudness envelope of the same audio, and after transcribing trim any word that starts or ends in 100 ms or more of quiet to its loud part (20 ms and 40 ms of padding), with the threshold set between the room noise and the voice.
A synthesized-speech test checks the whole path: words come back from SpeechAnalyzer in media time and a 1.5 s lead-in stays out of the first word.

title: Providers for Noto, Iconify, SVGL, Fontsource, Pexels, Pixabay, Freesound and ElevenLabs
Analysis jobs and MediaAnalysis
paragraphs: The seven analyses, each written into a private cache folder and committed only if the file didn't change meanwhile:

- thumbnails: a JPEG every 2 s at 320 px (keyframe tolerance keeps it fast), or one for an image
- waveform: mono peaks at 100 a second, Float32 file plus JSON header, placed by sample time so late-starting audio still lines up
- loudness: LoudnessMeter over the whole file
- proxy: 1080p all-intra HEVC through VTCompressionSession into AVAssetWriter untouched, every frame keeping its exact time and duration (each frame is encoded one late so its duration is known)
- transcript: SpeechAnalyzer en-US with word times in media time, fed a second of audio at a time from the file
- matte: accurate person segmentation plus the person-instance mask, added only inside holes of the closed person mask so a held mic stays while the instance mask's halo and the chair don't; greyscale 420f HEVC with the source frame times, three Vision workers, bounded queues
- isolatedVoice: AUSoundIsolation offline at 48 kHz, latency dropped from the front and fed as silence at the end, same length as the source

MediaAnalysis reads results synchronously from the cache, queues work with request/requestDefaults (proxies for video above 1080p; transcript, matte and voice for camera files; timeline media first), reports state per item and kind, and waits for results for callers that need them.

title: Decision-models recipe and real-project import test
paragraphs: The built-in recipe describes how decision-models went from EDL to its Filmora cut, read out of build_wfp.py and the scripts after it: the three record-it sessions, fix_cutoffs' loosened cuts, apply_v6's layout switch and transitions, add_gfx's graphics as take times, replace_sfx's sound rules, the per-section music cues and section names. ImportWriter saves an import with its report beside it. RealProjectTests (opt-in with TANDEM_REAL_MEDIA=1) rebuilds the video and checks it validates and survives a save and load.

title: Core Image compositor, effects, transitions, text and limiter
paragraphs: The per-frame layer pipeline (source, look, effects, crop, cutout, rounded corners, border, transform, drop shadow, opacity), runtime-compiled Metal kernels for colour, HSL and vignette, .cube LUTs, all eight transition types, Core Text titles with Mike's four presets and word captions, and the master true-peak limiter. Golden-pixel tests run the planner and composer with stand-in frames.

title: EDL importer for agent-cut takes
paragraphs: Rebuilds a video from a segment EDL plus a recipe: each segment of the take is placed with placeMedia (camera, voice and screen linked), the layout becomes a camera transform (full frame, or the cutout PiP), and the recipe adds the intro, loosened cuts, layout overrides, B-roll, graphics, cut and topic transitions with sounds on them, one music cue per section on alternating tracks, and section markers. Recipe times are take times, so everything lands on the same words whatever the cut.

title: Agent service, transcript tools, timeline dump and command schema
paragraphs: TandemService is the one request/response surface for HTTP, the CLI and MCP: status, media, timeline, transcript, search, pauses, tighten, apply (with dry runs), undo, redo, history, validate, frame, clip, export, loudness, watch and effects. Edits made with the project opened headless keep undo and idempotency history on disk. Commands are checked against a hand-written JSON schema so misspelt fields are errors.

title: Render Lottie stickers to HEVC with alpha (adds lottie-ios)
Import module with probe, media catalog and zip reader
paragraphs: Adds the TandemImport target. The shared pieces the importers build on: an import report that groups repeated findings, a builder that applies each import step through ProjectCoordinator and retries a rejected batch one command at a time, deterministic IDs, a media catalog that relinks moved files and keeps missing ones offline, an AVFoundation probe that stands in for MediaScanner.probe, and a small zip reader for .wfp files.

title: Normalise audio, animated images, WebM, SVG and fonts on import
Watch the project folder for new media
paragraphs: FolderWatcher follows the folder recursively with FSEvents and reports media files added, changed or removed, as project-relative paths, ignoring skipped folders and non-media files. Events are debounced and a file is only reported once it has stopped changing for a settle time, so a take record-it is still writing is reported once, when it's finished. Paths match whether the project uses /var or the real /private/var.

title: Analysis cache and job scheduler
paragraphs: AnalysisCache keeps each result in .tandem/cache/<kind>/<key>/ with an entry.json manifest, key = sha256(fingerprint|kind|version|settings). Jobs write into a private .tmp- folder that is renamed into place with the manifest already inside, so a crash never leaves a half result that lookups can see; stale temporaries are cleaned up later. Entries are evicted least recently used first past a size limit (50 GB default).

JobScheduler runs jobs by priority (interactive, timeline, background), then cheap kinds first, then oldest, within per-kind limits, a shared limit for proxy and matte, and a total. It dedupes by job ID (asking again can raise the priority), cancels cooperatively, throttles progress to observers, and lets a long job step aside at a checkpoint for more urgent work in its slot, resuming where it left off. Encoder jobs hold EncoderLock at background priority and hand it to a waiting export between frames.

title: Render layer maths and timeline plan
paragraphs: Shared placement maths (aspect fit, transform, orientation, crop, zoom to rectangle, format overrides) and a pure render plan: which media plays on which composition track, A/B alternation for centred transitions, instruction splits with layer stacks, and audio volume envelopes.

title: Timeline model, drag planning and the Premiere keymap
paragraphs: The pure half of the timeline, tested without a window: time to pixel maps with anchored zoom, lane layout (transcript, top video track down, then audio), snapping to edges, markers, the playhead and in/out, hit testing with edge grabs, and the drag planner that turns each tool's drag (move, Cmd-drag insert, trim, ripple trim, roll, slip, slide) into one EditBatch with limits, previewed on a copy of the project.

TimelineEdits builds the key and menu edits (lift and extract in to out, Q and W, blade at playhead, nudge, layout presets, link, markers, default dissolve, media drops). The keymap is JSON with Premiere-style defaults and user overrides. Adds the TandemAppTests target and the app's resource bundle.

title: Run the loudness meter through Accelerate
paragraphs: The per-sample meter took about 8 s of test time on seconds of audio in debug builds and would crawl through a 24 minute take. K-weighting now runs as one two-section vDSP biquad per channel, sub-block energy uses vDSP sums of squares, and true peak runs the four oversampling phases as vDSP convolutions carried across chunk boundaries. Results match the original per-sample meter (kept in the tests as the reference) to within 0.001 LU and 0.001 dB for any chunk size.

title: Catalogue with FTS5 search, licences, usage and favourites
Scan, probe and pair media in the project folder
paragraphs: MediaScanner walks the project folder (skipping .tandem, exports, node_modules, .build, .git, hidden folders and Filmora's .wfp.dir), fingerprints each file (size, mtime, SHA-256 of both ends) and probes it with AVFoundation: duration, rotated size, frame rate, audio, alpha and variable frame rate read from the sample table, so record-it screen recordings that hold frames for seconds show as VFR while a camera with a few dropped frames doesn't.

Known paths keep their IDs, renames are matched by content, unchanged files skip probing, and unreadable files (still being written) are reported instead of added. record-it takes pair by base name; offsets come from a <base>.take.json sidecar when there is one, otherwise from creation dates, treating sub-second gaps between whole-second stamps as rounding and clamping nonsense to 0 with a note.

title: Templates expand into linked clips
paragraphs: insertTemplate places a pack template (section card, Like and Subscribe, Comment Below) at a time, filling {{field}} placeholders and looking up template media by path, so packs don't need project media IDs.

title: Random edits must round-trip through JSON and undo
Layout presets and zoom-to-region commands
paragraphs: applyLayout sets full, PiP right, PiP left or split on video clips with Mike's Filmora values (50% at (0.87, 0.77), cutout, default drop shadow). zoomToRegion fills the frame with part of a screen recording, either static or as an eased zoom at a timeline time.

title: Loudness meter and shared encoder lock
paragraphs: BS.1770-4 / EBU R128 meter (integrated, loudness range, true peak) for per-file analysis and the export's master pass, and an encoder lock so proxy builds and exports take turns on the hardware encoder.

title: Core edit engine, module contracts and V1 plan
paragraphs: Adds tools/tandem, a native macOS editor meant to replace Filmora for the Convex videos. This first commit is the base the module work builds on:

- TandemCore: flick-based time, the project model with lenient JSON decoding, edit commands applied atomically by ProjectCoordinator with undo, revisions, idempotency and a seeded journal for crash recovery.
- Ripple modes per track (cut, follow, off) so tightening pauses cuts the take and lets B-roll, music and markers follow.
- Blade, trim, ripple trim, roll, slip, slide, speed, move, lift, extract, insert, close gap, transitions with handle checks, effects, keyframes.
- Contracts for media, render and the project session, plus build scripts.
